chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran who linked up this tradition:
“Gold and silver are two perverting metals. Whoever loves them is with them.”
The compiler of this book - may God increase his honor - interprets this to mean that whoever loves them so much that he doesn’t pay the Divinely Ordained dues on them is with them.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of gold and silver in Shia hadith regarding khums and attachment?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq employs the metaphor of 'perverting stones' to illustrate how gold and silver, when loved excessively, can distort one's spiritual orientation and lead to the neglect of divine dues like khums and zakat. This interpretation aligns with the Shia scholarly tradition of viewing wealth not as inherently evil, but as a test that perverts the heart when it becomes an idol preventing the fulfillment of religious obligations.

“Gold and silver are two perverting metals. Whoever loves them is with them.”
The compiler of the book - may God increase his honor - interprets this to mean that whoever loves them so much that he doesn’t pay the Divinely Ordained dues on them is with them.
